groups.title: Customary-present nominalization foundation
groups.proposal: Treat customary-present agentive formation as a typed nominalization of an owner-issued active customary-present VNC Result. Preserve the complete predicate and distinguish simple reanalysis from the fuller nominal transformation without using example verbstems as route permission.
groups.readingJob: Show the source VNC, predicate-to-nounstem change, agentive meaning, and the difference between reanalysis and full nominalization.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses nominalization and the intended degree only when both are genuinely available; the application preserves the typed VNC and derives everything fixed by that choice.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add example-stem, copied-predicate, formula, or surface controls.

groups.title: Customary-present agentive by reanalysis
groups.proposal: Convert the complete customary-present predicate into the restricted-use nounstem of an absolutive agentive NNC. Preserve projective and reflexive objects inside the nounstem, keep ni as its final constituent, and carry the source subject and class-conditioned number behavior without restricting the route to listed stems.
groups.readingJob: Show internal objects and reflexives, final ni, subject and number continuity, Source shape evidence, and examples as proof rather than admission.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended nominalization and any genuinely open participant interpretation; the application derives internal placement, final ni, and licensed number realization.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add manual ni placement, object movement, class ending, example-stem, or formula controls.

groups.title: Fully nominal customary-present agentive paradigm
groups.proposal: Build the fully nominal customary-present agentive NNC from the reanalyzed nounstem by using the canonical NNC state, subject, possessor, number, and noun-class owners. Preserve the agentive Source through absolutive and possessive singular and plural forms and compatible continuations.
groups.readingJob: Show state, subject, possessor, number dyads, noun class, internal agentive Source, and the relationship between restricted and fully nominal forms.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses intended state, subject, possessor, and number where they are real grammatical choices; the application derives agreement, allomorphy, boundaries, and compatible forms.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse normal NNC controls and do not add lesson-specific paradigm, suffix, example, or copied-stem choices.

groups.title: Customary meaning and preterit-agentive contrast
groups.proposal: Keep customary-present and preterit agentives structurally distinct even when their translations overlap, and preserve the licensed use of a preterit-agentive stem to complete a possessive paradigm.
groups.readingJob: Show habitual, continuing-relation, punctual, lexicalized, and overlapping readings together with the actual Source analysis.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses a genuinely intended analysis when context leaves it open; the application never decides from English translation alone.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not merge identical translations or surface forms, and do not generalize lexical meanings.

groups.title: Customary-present patientive NNCs
groups.proposal: Nominalize an owner-issued passive customary-present VNC Result as a patientive NNC while preserving passive structure, shuntline reflexive evidence, protected vowel quantity, the lack of projective objects, and the restriction against possessive state.
groups.readingJob: Show patient or undergoer meaning, worthy-of-treatment extension, passive Source, shuntline reflexive, protected quantity, state restriction, and contrasts with potential-patient and instrumentive formations.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended patientive meaning only where context leaves a real alternative; passive consequences and state restrictions are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not allow free possessive state, projective objects, example admission, or confusion with instrumentive and potential-patient routes.

groups.title: Instrumentive NNC two-source foundation
groups.proposal: Build the instrumentive paradigm from two typed nominalization paths: an impersonal customary-present source for absolutive state and an active imperfect source whose subject becomes the possessor for possessive state.
groups.readingJob: Show instrument, faculty, and means readings; the two source tenses and voices; subject continuity or subject-to-possessor transformation; and reflexive shuntline conversion.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended state and instrumentive meaning; the application selects and validates the required source pathway.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not synthesize one stem from the other or expose subject-to-possessor conversion as a manual operation.

groups.title: Instrumentive realizations and Source-shape variants
groups.proposal: Apply the two instrumentive pathways productively across typed Source shapes, including object-bearing, nonactive, supportive-vowel, reflexive, and hua or hua-lō variants, while keeping lexicalized readings typed and narrow.
groups.readingJob: Show the exact Source boundaries, voice and tense pathway, participants, vowel behavior, hua variants, compositional meaning, and lexicalized result.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses a genuine licensed variant or lexical reading; predictable Source-shape effects are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not whitelist the displayed stems and do not turn lexical meanings into productive shape rules.

groups.title: Present-agentive NNCs
groups.proposal: Convert a typed present-indicative VNC predicate into the restricted present-agentive nounstem and enforce its absolutive-state distribution while preserving reflexive, lexical, and Source-shape distinctions.
groups.readingJob: Show present Source, predicate reanalysis, agentive or property reading, state restriction, reflexive structure, and lexical distinctions.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended licensed reading only where it is genuinely ambiguous; state and structural realization are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not allow possessive state or authorize the route by the listed examples.

groups.title: Restricted and general-use future agentives
groups.proposal: Nominalize an active future VNC Result into a restricted stem ending in z and a general-use z-cā stem, preserve the original participant structure, derive singular qui and plural qu-eh, and pass the general-use Source into possessive and compound continuations.
groups.readingJob: Show future z, singular and plural number dyads, cā general use, possessive and compound continuations, participant structure, and narrow lexical meanings.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses nominalization and intended compatible continuation; z, cā, number realization, and participant preservation are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add manual z, cā, qui, qu-eh, example-stem, or copied-result controls.

groups.title: Action NNC taxonomy
groups.proposal: Represent action NNCs as typed nominalizations that can name an action, process, event, resultant state, instance, or result, while keeping passive-action and active-action kinds distinct.
groups.readingJob: Show the action-family meaning range and the passive versus active division.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses an intended meaning only where context leaves it open; voice and Source facts determine the structural family.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not turn the English label action into a universal meaning or merge active and passive structures.

groups.title: Passive-action NNCs
groups.proposal: Create the general-use passive-action stem from a passive distant-past VNC predicate ending in ca, transform the source subject into the possessor, and create the restricted absolutive stem with the licensed yō-tl matrix while preserving cā, internal objects, common number, and Subclass 1-B structure.
groups.readingJob: Show passive perspective, distant-past ca or protected cā, subject-to-possessor change, internal participants, yō-tl matrix, state distribution, number, and action or result readings.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses state and genuinely open meaning; the application derives the appropriate general or restricted structure.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add manual tense-shape, possessor-conversion, yō, noun-class, or example controls.

groups.title: Active-action NNC foundation
groups.proposal: Keep nominalized active-action NNCs distinct from derived active-action NNCs and license the nominalized family normally from intransitive distant-past Sources, with the narrow reflexive-object transitive path preserved as typed structure.
groups.readingJob: Show nominalization versus derivation, active versus passive action, normal intransitive Source, and the restricted reflexive transitive allowance.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended nominalized or derived family; the application validates voice, valence, and reflexive compatibility.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not infer route permission from example identity or treat all transitive sources as active-action compatible.

groups.title: General-use active-action NNCs
groups.proposal: Create the possessive-state general-use active-action stem from a distant-past active predicate ending in ca, convert a source subject to the possessor, convert mainline reflexive to shuntline ne, preserve Subclass 1-B behavior, and keep lexicalized means or result readings typed.
groups.readingJob: Show distant-past ca, subject-to-possessor change, reflexive shuntline, noun class, possessive distribution, compositional action, and licensed lexical shifts.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses intended possession and any genuinely open lexical reading; structural transformations are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not expose ca, reflexive conversion, possessor conversion, or class as lesson-specific choices and do not generalize lexical shifts.

groups.title: Restricted-use active-action NNCs
groups.proposal: Build the absolutive restricted-use active-action compound from the general-use cā Source and the licensed yō-tl matrix, preserving common nonhuman number and the full action, state, means, source, or result interpretation range.
groups.readingJob: Show cā protection, yō-tl matrix, absolutive distribution, common number, Source continuity, and compositional versus lexical readings.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses intended state and a genuinely open reading; the application derives the compound and all fixed morphology.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add manual cā, yō, matrix, class, or example choices.

groups.title: Active-action versus preterit-agentive contrast
groups.proposal: Keep possessive active-action and preterit-agentive Sources distinct even when their surface phonology is identical: the former contains distant-past ca and belongs to Subclass 1-B, while the latter contains preterit Ø plus the cā matrix and belongs to Subclass 1-A.
groups.readingJob: Show ca versus Ø-cā, Subclass 1-B versus 1-A, action or result versus agent meaning, identical-surface warning, and continuation consequences.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended Source analysis when context leaves a genuine ambiguity; the application preserves the compatible class and continuation path.
groups.controlPolicy: Never reconstruct Source from the surface string or merge the two analyses because their output sounds alike.
